questions.q: What are the three parts of a role assignment?
options: A user or group account, a role definition, and a securable item
A password, a role definition, and an expiration date
A report, a dataset, and a data source
A folder, a schedule, and a subscription
questions.explain: A role assignment maps who (user/group) is allowed to do what (a role definition's permitted tasks) to which item (the securable item).

questions.q: Why are item-level and system-level role assignments described as mutually exclusive?
options: Item-level controls access to folder-hierarchy content; system-level authorizes server-wide operations not tied to any item — neither grants what the other does
Because a user can only ever have one type of role assignment, period
Because system-level assignments override and replace item-level ones automatically
Because item-level assignments are only for administrators
questions.explain: They cover fundamentally different scopes, which is why granting a new user full access typically requires creating both.

questions.q: What happens to security settings when you create a new subfolder under Home?
options: It inherits the role assignments of its parent folder by default
It starts with no security at all until an admin assigns some
It automatically gets the Content Manager role for every user
It copies the security settings of the most recently modified report
questions.explain: Role assignments are inherited down the folder hierarchy from Home unless you customize security on a specific item.

questions.q: What does "Customize security" do on an item's Security page?
options: Breaks inheritance so you can create a role assignment scoped to that item alone
Deletes every role assignment on the server
Converts item-level security into system-level security
Merges the item's security with every other item in the same folder
questions.explain: Customizing security overrides the inherited assignment with one specific to that single item, without affecting siblings.

questions.q: Which predefined role would you assign to most users who only need to view and run reports?
options: Browser
Content Manager
Publisher
System Administrator
questions.explain: Browser grants view/run access with nothing more — Content Manager and Publisher are reserved for a much smaller group.
